headline: Tk 20 crore gold seized: 80 gold bars found under seats of FlyDubai plane
summary: Dhaka Customs recovered approximately 9.33 kg of gold bars hidden under aircraft seats at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport.
details: Dhaka Customs House has seized 80 gold bars from a FlyDubai flight at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport. The gold, weighing approximately 9.33 kg, has an estimated market value of around Tk 20 crore.

The operation was carried out on Wednesday night around 10 PM based on secret intelligence. A team from the Customs House, accompanied by intelligence agencies and other authorities, conducted a thorough search of the aircraft.
The gold bars were found wrapped in scotch tape and hidden beneath the seats of the plane.
Customs officials stated that legal proceedings are currently underway to address the incident.

headline_marked: Asif Mahmud [[demands retraction of ACC allegations]] within 24 hours
headline: Asif Mahmud demands retraction of ACC allegations within 24 hours
summary: The former advisor and NCP spokesperson claims the corruption charges are politically motivated and lack evidence, threatening a defamation lawsuit.
details: Former advisor and National Citizens Party (NCP) spokesperson Asif Mahmud Sajeeb Bhuiyan has demanded the retraction of news reports based on statements from the Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) spokesperson within 24 hours.
Speaking at a press conference on Wednesday, Mahmud called the reports 'formulaic' and claimed they lacked specific information and did not align with the ACC's own allegations.
He denied corruption charges related to promotion and transfer trades, stating that all promotions were carried out through the proper legal process and the Public Service Commission (PSC).
Mahmud alleged that he is being framed for political reasons and that the published information is largely untrue, causing him social and political defamation.

He pointed out that an ACC deputy director had initially mentioned the preliminary truth of the allegations to a media outlet but later requested via WhatsApp not to publish the matter, suggesting a lack of solid evidence.
Mahmud warned of legal action against those involved if the ACC and media outlets do not take steps to retract the reports within the given timeframe.

He compared these actions to the 'old tactics' of the previous Awami League government, claiming he is being harassed politically in the same way the party had targeted Khaleda Zia with corruption cases.
caption:
